question.text: The operations desk at Chambal Managed Futures Fund has detected a cyber-incident — unauthorised access to its fund-administrator portal. Under the CSCRF framework and CERT-In directions applicable to SEBI-regulated entities, what is the mandatory incident-reporting timeline?

answer.text: Within 6 hours of noticing or being brought to notice

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that any incident on cyber-security risk must be reported to the sector regulator and central government within 6 hours, and confirms that the CSCRF applies to AIFs by manager category, so a Cat III AIF manager is squarely within scope of the 6-hour reporting clock. The Trap: 24 hours and 72 hours are common data-protection style timelines rather than the cyber-incident timeline applicable here, and a 7-day window is far longer than the workbook prescribes. Note: Based on Series-XIX-E workbook p.163 (6-hour cyber-incident reporting) and p.290 (CSCRF applicability to AIFs by manager category).
